Thanks again for the call today — quick recap and a few clarifying questions from our side.

Key pain points we mentioned:
- Current endpoint (self-hosted, single AZ) has frequent p95 spikes (~800–1200ms) under bursty traffic.
- Cache misses and cold starts on long-context inference (up to 8k tokens) are killing tail latency.
- Cost unpredictability when bursts hit during peak robotics operations.

Primary goals:
- Target p50 per-token latency <= 50ms for our 13B model across steady-state requests.
- p95 <= 200ms for typical prompt sizes (<=512 tokens).
- Support sustained throughput of ~200 QPS (short prompts) with ability to absorb 2x short bursts.
- Private deployment (VPC) in us-east-1, full audit logs and SOC2 evidence for procurement.

Notes / asks:
- Can you confirm whether Redwood can meet the 50ms p50 target for LLM-13B quantized at ~4 concurrent streams per GPU?
- What topology would you recommend (dedicated pools, autoscale policy, KV-cache placement)?
- Please send a short recap of the latency-throughput SLOs and any suggested next steps.

I've attached our requirements PDF (acme-reqs.pdf). Procurement will need SOC2 evidence later (adding them on next reply).

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Liu
Head of ML, Acme Robotics

Hi Sara — great speaking with you. Below is a short technical recap and recommended next steps based on the goals you outlined.

Recap of pain & goals (as I captured them)
- Tail latency from cold starts and large context (<= 8192 tokens) is the main blocker.
- Goal: p50 per-token <= 50ms; p95 <= 200ms for typical 512-token prompts; sustained throughput 200 QPS with 2x burst handling.
- Private VPC deployment in us-east-1; SOC2 evidence required for procurement.

Redwood recommendation (high level)
- Deployment topology: Dedicated GPU pool (reserved capacity) in us-east-1 with 3 active workers, 2 standby (fast cold-start fallback). Use autoscale policy that scales by queue depth with a 60s warm-up window.
- Runtime optimizations: quantized LLM-13B (8-bit / Q4_0 where feasible), KV-cache pinned in memory on serving nodes, prefix caching for common instruction prompts, and continuous batching for steady-state.
- Latency expectations: With the above config and model quantization we estimate p50 per-token in the 30–55ms range for short prompts; p95 depends on prompt length but should be <= 200ms for <=512 tokens. For long-context (4k–8k tokens) expect higher tail latency; recommend a staged rollout to characterize.
- Fallback policy: automatic fallback to an LLM-6B quantized variant for non-critical or lower-precision requests to preserve p95 SLOs under extreme load.
- Observability & SLOs: we will enable token-level latency breakdowns and per-route dashboards; recommend a 2-week canary with synthetic traffic to validate p95 under realistic loads.

Attachments I'm sharing:
- latency-slo-table.csv (simple SLO matrix, p50/p95 budgets by prompt size)
- redwood-deployment-proposal.pdf (high-level topology + cost ballpark)

Next steps
1) Confirm the SLO targets above and accept the proposed canary approach.
2) Share any additional compliance docs you need (we'll route SOC2 evidence to procurement).
3) Schedule a 60-min technical deep-dive next week to walk infra and test plan (I can bring our infra lead Vivek).

Proposed times (PDT): Wed 21 Apr 10:00–11:00, Wed 21 Apr 14:00–15:00, Thu 22 Apr 09:00–10:00.

If that looks good I'll run the MLP and share a Mutual Action Plan.

Hi Sara (and Acme procurement) — quick answers and confirm the meeting.

- Canary: 2-week canary with traffic shaping is exactly what we recommend — start with 10% production traffic ramping to 50% over 48 hours under synthetic load validation. We'll include a rollback playbook.
- Fallback lifecycle: The LLM-6B fallback is deployed as a compatible model variant behind the same API surface. Routing is policy-driven in our control plane — switching to the fallback is a routing rule change (no client-side changes required).
- Ballpark cost: Dedicated reserved pool (3 active + 2 standby GPUs in us-east-1) + storage & networking is roughly $35k–$50k/month depending on exact instance types and egress. We’ll provide a more detailed breakdown for procurement.
